title: The Cipher of Vienna
premise: Freya Yarrow, a crash investigator whose family died in row twelve of Flight 447, has spent seven years hiding under a polished lie and a packed go-bag. When the safe house he's lived in is listed for sale with interior photos, he realizes someone inside the network that trained him is hunting him — and the listing itself is a message. To survive, Freya must turn his skills against the Cipher, the Vienna-based cell that made him invisible, while an unlikely found family of fellow ghosts helps him choose truth over loyalty. In the end, he burns the network's archive at a border checkpoint, testifies to what really happened in row twelve, and finally unpacks the go-bag.
about_author: Sebastian Coldharbour is the pen name of a former aviation insurance analyst who spent a decade reading crash reports before turning to fiction. He writes from a different city each year, a habit he insists is research rather than paranoia.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Opening on the anniversary of the crash, Freya recites his cover story at a support group for survivors' families, lying fluently about who he is. The emotional beat is grief worn as performance — we see the go-bag by the door and understand invisibility is his religion.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. A routine search reveals his safe house on a real estate site: twelve photos, including his hidden wall safe and the false floor panel. Someone photographed the inside while he slept. Panic drives him to grab the go-bag — but he stays, because leaving means admitting they've found him.

chapters.title: The Handler's Voicemail
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. A voicemail in an old training cipher offers him 'retirement assistance.' He decodes it in a laundromat and realizes the message predates the listing by three days — they wanted him to run so they could follow. First appearance of Mara, a locksmith who notices him sweating over a padlock.

chapters.title: Mara
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara Kessler, a former network courier now living openly, recognizes Freya's tradecraft when he sweeps her shop for bugs. She confronts him not with betrayal but with coffee and a question: 'Who trained you to be this afraid?' The beat is the first crack in his isolation.

chapters.title: The Cipher of Vienna
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Flashback chapter: eight years ago, Freya — then a grieving crash investigator recruited by the network — learned how grief makes people erasable. We learn the network faked evidence about row twelve to bury a maintenance scandal, and Freya's silence was purchased with his new identity.

chapters.title: Open House
chapters.summary: Freya and Mara's POVs alternating. They attend the safe house's open house posing as buyers, discovering the agent is a network cutout and the 'seller' signature belongs to a man dead since 2019. Freya finds a micro-camera still transmitting. Emotional beat: rage sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Go-Bag Problem
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya audits his own life like a crash scene: every habit, every route, catalogued for compromise. He realizes the network didn't find him — someone sold him. Suspicion falls on Tomas, his longtime dead-drop contact, and loyalty begins curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Dead Drop
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Tomas Varga, aging and indebted, confesses to the reader (not yet to Freya) that he traded Freya's file to pay medical debts for his daughter. His chapters humanize the betrayer. Beat: guilt as its own kind of surveillance.

chapters.title: Found Family
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara introduces Freya to her circle: Anselm, a forger; Priya, a disgraced journalist chasing the Flight 447 story; and quiet old Ivo, who keeps everyone's secrets in a notebook. For one evening, Freya eats dinner with people who know his real name. Beat: belonging, terrifying and warm.

chapters.title: What the Black Box Never Said
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya shares her suppressed investigation: the row-twelve passengers were seated there deliberately — witnesses to something. Freya cross-references her passenger list against network personnel files and goes white: his own recruitment was part of the cover-up.

chapters.title: Checkpoint
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya learns the network rotates border checkpoint staff at midnight Sunday — a narrow window when the hunt list isn't synced. He plans extraction for himself alone, then looks at the dinner table photo Mara took and can't leave them off it. Beat: loyalty vs. survival.

chapters.title: The Archive Beneath the Danube
chapters.summary: Anselm's POV. Anselm reveals the network keeps physical records — the Archive — in a flooded cold-storage vault under Vienna. Every erased person, every forged report, including the true Flight 447 data. Burning it would free the ghosts; keeping it could convict them. Debate becomes the chapter's engine.

chapters.title: Tomas Comes In
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Tomas, drowning in guilt, warns Freya that the network moved up the timeline: the checkpoint shift changes Saturday, not Sunday, and a cleaner named Herr Falk is already in Vienna. Tomas offers himself as bait. Beat: betrayal answered with fragile trust.

chapters.title: Falk
chapters.summary: Falk's POV. Inside the antagonist: Falk doesn't hate Freya; he pities him, seeing 'unresolved assets' as loose threads to be tidied. Through Falk we learn the network's chilling self-image as janitors of history. Beat: dread through competence — the hunter is calm, methodical, almost kind.

chapters.title: The Notebook
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Falk raids Mara's circle; Ivo swallows the notebook's most dangerous page and lets himself be taken so the others can scatter. Freya watches from across the street, go-bag in hand, and chooses to stay. Beat: sacrifice reframing what family costs.

chapters.title: Interrogation of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. In custody, Ivo outlasts Falk with silence and misdirection, buying forty-eight hours. Meanwhile Freya and Priya reconstruct the Archive's access protocol from a child's mnemonic Ivo once taught Mara. Beat: the oldest member protecting the youngest network — the found one.

chapters.title: Saturday
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The plan compresses: enter the vault during a power-swap window, copy the Flight 447 originals, burn the rest, reach the checkpoint before the midnight shift change. Tomas creates a diversion that will likely cost him. Beat: no more hiding — Freya walks toward the fire instead of away.

chapters.title: The Vault
chapters.summary: Freya and Mara's POVs. In the flooded archive, Freya finds his own file — and his family's, revealing his recruitment was engineered the week after the funeral. Mara pulls him out of paralysis as the incendiaries tick. Beat: the lie he polished was written by others; the truth is his to take back.

chapters.title: Fire on the Water
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The Archive burns beneath the Danube as Falk arrives too late, watching years of leverage go up in steam. Tomas's diversion works but he's captured. Freya escapes with the black-box originals sewn into his coat. Beat: catharsis and cost in equal measure.

chapters.title: Midnight Shift Change
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. At the border checkpoint, minutes before the shift change, Falk intercepts Freya — not with violence but with an offer: disappear forever, keep the pension, stay a ghost. Freya answers by handing him a copy of the row-twelve file and walking through anyway. Beat: the climax is a choice, not a fight.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The originals reach aviation authorities and Priya's story runs: row twelve, the maintenance scandal, the network named. Ivo is released; Tomas takes a deal; Falk vanishes, unemployed by history. Freya gives testimony under his real name for the first time in eight years. Beat: truth as the only home left.

chapters.title: Unpacked
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Months later, Freya visits the rebuilt memorial where row twelve's names are read aloud, standing with Mara, Priya, Anselm, and Ivo. At home, he finally empties the go-bag — toothbrush, cash, the old cipher card — and packs the drawer instead with photographs. Final beat: belonging chosen, not performed.
